newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to offer credit, cut tariffs on telcoms.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to offer credit, cut tariffs on telcoms.

text.p: Brazil will introduce low-cost credit lines and cut import tariffs to help stimulate investment in the telecommunications sector, Communications Minister Sergio Motta said.

The government would gradually introduce credit lines for private telecommunications investments via the national banking system, offering internationally competitive interest rates, Motta told at a seminar on telecommunications privatization.

Overseas capital might also be involved -- Japan's Eximbank had provisionally agreed to provide about $2.0 billion in financing for telecommunications joint-ventures involving Brazilian and Japanese companies, the minister said.
Planning Minister Antonio Kandir was due to discuss the credit idea during an upcoming visit to Tokyo, he added.
Regarding imports, the government would announce next week the elimination of a 20 percent tariff on imported components for cellular telephone transmission systems, Motta said.
